newsitem.title: USA: U.S. swap spreads tighter at the very-long-end.
newsitem.headline: U.S. swap spreads tighter at the very-long-end.

text.p: Spreads on U.S. interest rate swaps tightened at the long-end over the past week, but the short-end was mostly unchanged, dealers said.
The tightening was most dramatic on very-long-term swaps, where spreads narrowed significantly after widening by the same amount the previous week.

As has happened frequently in the past, the Treasury's auction of new 30-year bonds distorted swap spreads when a sizable yield gap developed between the on-the-run and when-issued bonds, dealers said.
The new 30-year bond auctioned November 7 settled November 15. Spreads on 30-year swaps, which had jumped to about 40 basis points, narrowed to about 35.
Spreads on 15-year swaps narrowed by two to three basis points. Spreads were quoted at about 49 basis points over the 10-year note.

At 10-years, there was much less movement. Spreads have been stuck in a very narrow range, around 31 basis points, for weeks. Heavy Eurobond issuance swapped to floating rates and a generally bullish investor outlook on interest rates have kept a lid on the 10-year spread, dealers said.
